The Cholesky Solver

Source: R/solver.R
solve_chol.Rd

Selects a Cholesky decomposition of the assembled penalized information \(X^\top W X + S\) for the scoring step of iwls(). The information is formed explicitly, so the condition number of the system is squared; a matrix that is not positive definite has its eigenvalues floored, at the relative level floor, before it is factored. The decomposition names no coordinate, so none is reported as aliased. It is the route that solve_qr() and solve_svd() follow where the square root of the curvature does not exist.

iwls_solvers compares it with the other two solvers.

Usage

solve_chol(floor = 1e-08)

Arguments

floor

The relative floor of the eigenvalues, a single positive number. A penalized matrix that is not positive definite is rebuilt from its eigendecomposition with every eigenvalue below floor times the largest absolute eigenvalue raised to that level. The default is 1e-8.

Value

An S7 object of class SolveChol, which inherits from IwlsSolver, with the property floor.

See also

solve_qr() and solve_svd() for the other solvers; iwls_solvers for the comparison; iwls() for the function that takes the object.

Examples

solve_chol()
#> Cholesky solver (floor 1e-08)
solve_chol(floor = 1e-10)
#> Cholesky solver (floor 1e-10)

set.seed(1)
dd <- data.frame(x = runif(120, -2, 2))
dd$y <- sin(1.4 * dd$x) + rnorm(120, sd = 0.3)
G <- distributions7::gaussian1_distrib()
fit <- statmod(y ~ s(x, bspline_smooth(k = 8)), G, dd,
               inner_optimizer = iwls(solver = solve_chol(floor = 1e-10)))
fit@methods$smooth
#> iwls: chol, expected information (the observed after 10 iterations)
#>   maxit 1000, tol 1e-06
